candidate.blueprint_topic: Safety and Infection Prevention and Control — Standard Precautions
candidate.educational_objective: Apply Standard Precautions to every patient in every healthcare setting and select PPE according to the anticipated exposure risk for the task.

options.A: Use Standard Precautions only when infection is known or suspected, adding Transmission-Based Precautions if the organism requires them.
options.B: Use Standard Precautions only for tasks with anticipated blood or body-fluid exposure, not for routine bedside care.
options.C: Use Standard Precautions routinely in inpatient units, while outpatient settings rely mainly on diagnosis-specific precautions.
options.D: Use Standard Precautions for every client in every healthcare setting, including hand hygiene and task-based PPE selected according to anticipated exposure.

candidate.rationale: CDC Core Infection Prevention and Control Practices state that Standard Precautions apply to all patient care, regardless of suspected or confirmed infectious status, and across all healthcare settings. They include hand hygiene and selection of PPE based on the nature of the interaction and the anticipated risk of exposure to blood, body fluids, infectious material, mucous membranes, non-intact skin, or contaminated equipment. Transmission-Based Precautions are added when indicated; they do not replace Standard Precautions.
candidate.source_claim_supported: CDC states that Standard Precautions apply to all patient care in all healthcare settings regardless of infectious status and include hand hygiene plus PPE selected according to anticipated exposure.
candidate.source_document_title: CDC's Core Infection Prevention and Control Practices for Safe Healthcare Delivery in All Settings
candidate.source_locator: Core Practices table → Standard Precautions; 5a Hand Hygiene; PPE recommendations under Standard Precautions.
candidate.source_organization: Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC)
